lead.text: NASA commissioned a sixteen-member independent study team on UAP on 24 May 2022, chaired by the astrophysicist David Spergel. Its report of 14 September 2023 found no conclusive evidence in the peer-reviewed literature of an extraterrestrial origin, and named poorly calibrated sensors and missing metadata as the main obstacle to analysis.

record.text: The published report runs to 36 pages and was released on 14 September 2023.

The report says UAP are usually detected by chance, by sensors not designed or calibrated for the purpose and lacking metadata, and that with incomplete archiving the origin of many UAP remains uncertain; analysis is hampered by poor calibration, the lack of multiple measurements and missing sensor metadata.

It finds no conclusive evidence in the peer-reviewed literature of an extraterrestrial origin, but treats the question as legitimate, describing a continuum between searching for technologies of distant civilisations and looking for them closer to home.

It names stigma as an obstacle, noting that scientists avoid topics such as technosignatures that could damage their credibility and promotion prospects, and says NASA lending its name to the subject is already helping to reduce that stigma.

In the report's foreword, Associate Administrator Nicola Fox says NASA is appointing a Director of UAP Research to centralise communications and engage in the whole-of-government UAP initiative. At the briefing NASA did not name the appointee.
AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I lists the NASA team, June 2022 to September 2023, among the official US government UAP efforts it reviewed.
Team member Michael Gold, a former NASA associate administrator, testified as a named witness at the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024.

Canada's Chief Science Advisor cited the NASA study and its new director post as precedent in the Sky Canada report of June 2025, which recommends that pilots, cabin crew and air traffic controllers be encouraged to report UAP without fear of stigma.

summary.text: The team was chaired by Spergel with Daniel Evans as designated federal official. It began work on 24 October 2022, held one public meeting on 31 May 2023 and reported on 14 September 2023; its members included Capt. Scott Kelly, Anamaria Berea, Federica Bianco and David Grinspoon.

Its core recommendation was that NASA play a prominent role in a whole-of-government, evidence-based effort, using its Earth-observing satellites to probe the conditions around UAP detected by other means, alongside an enhanced Aviation Safety Reporting System for pilots, machine learning on curated data and smartphone-based citizen reporting.
With the report, NASA announced a Director of UAP Research without naming the appointee; a later statement identified Mark McInerney.

The study positioned NASA as a civil complement to the Pentagon's AARO within a whole-of-government framework, while acknowledging that much of the relevant military and intelligence data is classified.
